text: I decided, after being away from you for a long time, to come out and tell you where I had been hiding and how I pulled myself back from the grave.
What was the secret that made me feel as if I had my life back again after I had been told that I might have cancer, or that it was very likely?
The doctor thought I had cancer because I had many clear symptoms that, in his view, did not have another explanation.
Now, [clears throat], I am not young. I am in my fifties—53 years old—and throughout my life I have tried many diets.
I have spent most of my life dieting, and during the last five years my health kept getting worse.
It kept getting worse and worse, and I did not know why, even though I had been following diets for about four and a half to five years.
Since around 2019, and in between, I also tried the carnivore diet.
My health kept declining until I reached a stage where I was told I had an autoimmune condition that could suddenly affect the body. Doctors told me there was no solution except
procedures and an immune-modulating medication that I would have to receive in the hospital, which was difficult and had many side effects.
Then I went to my doctor. I live in Germany, as you know, so it was my Hausarzt, my family doctor.
I told him my head hurt badly and that I could barely move or walk. My blood pressure was extremely high.
It was around 190, with the lower reading above 90, and he told me I needed to go to the hospital immediately.
He told me to go straight to emergency care. I said no, I do not want to go into hospitals because my previous experiences had not been reassuring.
So he had me sign papers saying I was going home on my own responsibility, and he gave me devices to monitor my blood pressure and breathing at home.
I do not remember everything, but I wore the devices for two days, 48 hours, and he referred me to a cardiologist.
The cardiologist told me I had an enlarged heart. I was swollen all over, and my legs were so bad that I could hardly walk.
I could barely stand on my knees. Suddenly I felt as if I was finished.
In Germany they call it a Schlaflabor, a sleep laboratory. I was referred there and received a breathing device.
I had been using that breathing device for about three years. Exactly two years ago I went to Berlin with my family.
We went to attend a symphony. I showed you a photo before, and around that time
if I needed to go up or down stairs, I had to do it backwards because I could not do it normally.
I could not descend the stairs facing forward. I had to turn around and go down backwards to avoid the pain.
My brain no longer seemed able to coordinate properly with my leg—to bend the knee and place my foot on the next step while facing forward.
So I would walk backwards. My family would get upset and worried, especially my son, because I was very ill.
I was extremely, extremely ill.
I went to the doctor and told him I had blood in my urine and was going to the bathroom frequently at night. I also had diabetes, so he prescribed diabetes medication.
I started taking metformin. I was taking medication for diabetes, blood pressure, and cholesterol, which I was told was hereditary. Then I told him about the bleeding.
My urine was always red and contained blood. A kidney examination showed a cyst on one kidney.
He said the kidney cyst should not cause bleeding, so he thought the bleeding was probably from the bladder. Tests showed no infection, and he said that meant it could be cancer.
I said, 'Bladder cancer? There is no solution for that.' He told me that in some cases they remove a kidney or the bladder and use an external bag and tubing.
I asked him how long someone might live afterward. I understood him to say six months, and I asked again, 'Only six months?'
He then said some people had lived five or six years. I started crying. I went home and made a decision.
I decided I did not want any more stress. I stopped working and stopped everything in my life that caused stress.
I isolated myself, and my only concern became spending time with my son and family. I had not told them what the doctor had said.
At that stage, I started seeing them every day. We went out together during the summer.
Last summer we went swimming at the sea every day, and I tried to spend good time with them because, in my mind, I was saying goodbye.
I did not know how long I had until the endoscopy was done. In Germany, as you know, appointments can take a long time. I told my closest friends
what the doctor had told me and about my fears. They encouraged me and told me that people can sometimes recover.
I will never forget how they stood by me, and I am very grateful to them.
It was a very difficult period while I waited for the endoscopy and ultrasound appointments.
A few days before Ramadan, I had reached a point where I was asking
ChatGPT what I could eat that might reduce the pain and bleeding and help me sleep a little. It told me to stop protein
because of concerns about the kidneys. Then, by chance, I saw an interview on Zat Masr
with Dr. Diaa Al-Awady. I hope you will recite Al-Fatiha for him. May God have mercy on him.
I thought, 'What kind of doctor is this?' He was talking about religion, philosophy, science, and medicine, and it really caught my attention.
I could not stop watching. I had plenty of free time, so I watched video after video and podcast after podcast.
I began waiting for each new podcast to hear what he would talk about today or tomorrow. Then I went back to his older videos and studied them.
To this day I still study them. I go back to his channel, take notes, memorize points, and reread what he said.
At that time I first thought, 'This doctor is crazy.' But then I asked myself what I had to lose. I had tried almost every diet imaginable.
They had exhausted me, and my health had collapsed. I already felt as if I had one foot in the grave, so what did I have to lose?
I had hardly ever eaten potatoes because they caused constipation for me, and I could never tolerate sugar.
If I even smelled sugar or honey, I felt as though my body reacted badly, and I would become ill. I will explain what used to happen to me.
I said, 'What do I have to lose?' Look at my nails now. For twenty years they had been so soft that they would bleed.
They were so soft they would tear deep into the flesh. I thought, what do I have to lose? I wanted to eat potatoes before I died.
I said I would follow his diet and see the results. Since he was so confident in his system, I decided
to record everything on paper every single day starting from March 1, 2026.
Every day I wrote down my weight, health condition, pain, symptoms, exactly what I ate, the date, the time I ate, and how I reacted immediately afterward.
I also recorded how I felt one hour later, two hours later, and the next day. At first the table was random, but then it started to become organized.
After about ten days, I noticed something surprising while I was keeping the records and eating according to the plan.
I had expected to prove that this doctor was like the others and that the system would fail and make me even sicker.
But what I observed was that my weight started to go down, the swelling in my body began to disappear, and the fluid retention improved.
The swelling in my legs, hands, face, and neck went away. For an entire month I did not snore in my sleep, and I did not feel that my breathing stopped.
I had been using a breathing mask during sleep because of episodes where my breathing would stop and oxygen levels could fall.
I had been told that this could affect the brain and memory, so I was surprised by what I was noticing afterward.
The immune-type reactions and sensitivities I felt in my body seemed to disappear. Then the pain began to lessen, including my knee pain.
From March 1, 2026 until today, near the end of May 2026,
I can say that I was doing much better. I had not originally intended to stop my medications, by the way, but
I read foreign studies about cholesterol and came to believe that cholesterol treatment was being overstated, so I stopped that medication.
I looked at mortality figures and tried to compare the numbers for people taking cholesterol medication and those not taking it.
I believed the difference was small enough that I was willing to take the risk, so I stopped it and waited to see what happened.
This had been about a month and a half earlier. Then, after around 12 to 15 days,
I had imaging, an endoscopy, and an ultrasound of the kidneys. I went to the doctor, and she asked,
'Where is the kidney cyst?' I said, 'I do not know—you told me it would not disappear.' She said she could not find it and wondered if it had been on the other kidney.
She checked my file and examined the other kidney and said there was no cyst there either. Then I had the endoscopy, and I was told there was no bladder tumor.
I told her the bleeding had also disappeared. She asked how often I was getting up at night to use the bathroom, and I said, 'Not once.'
I was sleeping eight hours continuously. After only about 12 days, I could sleep through the night without getting up
to use the bathroom even once. She said that was unusual. I told her I knew. She asked if I had changed anything.
I said I had simply been focusing more carefully on my diet. She told me to continue what I was doing because the improvement seemed remarkable.
I went home very happy. At that point I told my family what the doctors had said and about my fear that
I might have cancer, because my family doctor had believed that, without a severe bladder infection,
persistent blood in the urine could indicate bladder cancer. I told them, 'I feel very well now.'
I told them that this had been my condition before, but that today I felt much better, thanks to God.
About twenty days ago, I stood up to get a glass of water and became dizzy.
I checked my blood pressure and saw it was dropping. I had already stopped the diabetes medication and cholesterol medication, and now my blood pressure was low.
I normally had very high blood pressure. So I decided that the next morning I would skip one blood pressure pill and monitor what happened during the day.
Every hour or two I measured my blood pressure. If it dropped or rose too much, I planned to take the pill immediately.
On the first day my blood pressure was normal. On the second day it was normal as well.
For the entire first week it stayed normal. Now it has been around 15 to 20 days with normal readings. Even the veins in my hands
which had been almost invisible started to become noticeable again.
When I used to have blood drawn, they would puncture my hands repeatedly, my hands would bruise, and they could hardly find a vein.
Recently I went for blood tests, and drawing the blood was the easiest it had ever been.
Even the needle mark was barely noticeable. Thank God, I was told that all of my test results were within normal ranges.
Today I feel healthier, stronger, and more energetic.
I also feel happier and more refreshed, and I am still continuing with the approach.
I am very happy with it. Giving up eggs and chicken was difficult because I love both of them. I used to drive two hours
to a farm outside the city to buy free-range eggs, chicken, and milk
directly from local farms. I even made traditional fermented foods myself because I was focused on the microbiome.
I tried almost everything to regain my health. I came to believe that the approach of the late doctor was what helped me.
May God have mercy on him and fill his soul with light.
For me, it also involved fasting. I became able to fast for as long as 23 hours out of 24, using intermittent fasting.
I can drink juice without feeling guilty, and I eat rice and potatoes without feeling guilty. I also eat meat
and fish, but I now try to choose wild-caught fish rather than farmed fish, and I usually try to choose organic meat.
I try to buy organic food as much as I can. I also eat sugar and enjoy many foods that I had avoided before.
A week ago, my son bought me a Chupa Chups lollipop, and I ate a lollipop for the first time in my life.
This is not an advertisement. I simply felt incredibly happy that I could eat a lollipop or sweets without immediately feeling ill.
I am also eating jam and honey.
I put vinegar and olive oil on potatoes. To me, it feels like healthy, satisfying, enjoyable food.
Life feels good. Maybe this system will turn out like the diets before it and the improvement will not last—I do not know.
But from my own perspective, I took the chance and I feel recovered. Today I feel in very good health, thanks to God, and I wish the same health
and well-being for everyone I love and for all of you.
My only wish is that, if I continue this way for the rest of my life, God will
grant me a long life, strength, and health—and the same for you and everyone we love.
To hell with money, harmful foods, industries, medications, and everything that profits from illness.
And to anyone who benefits while knowing something is harmful but does not tell you to stop the harm.
I am not encouraging anyone to follow this system. I am only speaking from my own experience: I did not die when I stopped eating eggs and chicken.
I did not die when I ate potatoes, and I did not die when I ate rice. Those who follow the system strictly
also stop vegetables and salads, and they may notice a difference. Yesterday I was at a restaurant and ordered a piece of tuna with
boiled potatoes. Here in Germany people really like Kartoffeln—potatoes—so ordering potatoes is completely normal.
There was a man sitting across from me with a plate full of salad and a large belly. I almost wanted to go over to him.
He was German, and I wanted to tell him, 'Eat potatoes and leave the salad that, in my opinion, is upsetting your intestines and not helping you lose weight.'
Then I thought I would tell all of you instead. Maybe the message will reach someone and have an effect.
Maybe a small butterfly effect can spread and lead to greater awareness and better health.
Think back to the period before the First World War and look at old photographs. You will see that hospitals were not always crowded except in wartime or emergencies.
There were not large numbers of patients waiting on stairs and in corridors except during war
or epidemics. In my view, epidemics became more frequent with industrialization compared with earlier times.
In earlier centuries, major outbreaks such as plague or cholera occurred only occasionally, and hospitals were often much less crowded.
They were mainly used for special cases such as fractures. I also felt that my memory improved; before, I could barely put two words together, and I withdrew
because I was so ill. But I missed you very much, I love you very much, and may God have mercy on Dr.
Al-Awady. Please recite Al-Fatiha for him.
